why: Every figure here is quoted from its source, linked, and kept in this file rather than typed into the page.

facts.claim: of Americans whose large appliance broke in the last five years replaced it rather than repairing it.
facts.quote: 60% of respondents had an appliance stop working in the last five years, and of those, 58% of them ended up replacing the broken product.
facts.source: Consumer Reports, Right to Repair Survey of 2,154 U.S. adults, summer 2024

facts.claim: of the people who replaced it had tried to repair it first, and could not.
facts.quote: Of those that ended up replacing their product, 26% tried to repair it but couldn't.
facts.source: Consumer Reports, Right to Repair Survey, 2024

facts.claim: appliance makers examined made their service manuals available.
facts.quote: Of the 50 appliance manufacturers examined, just seven made service manuals available.
facts.source: U.S. PIRG, iFixit and Repair.org, investigation submitted to the FTC

facts.claim: of major appliances went to landfill in the United States in 2018.
facts.quote: leaving 2.1 million tons of appliances to be landfilled.
facts.source: U.S. EPA, Durable Goods: Product-Specific Data
